newsitem.title: UK: Major pleads with Protestant extremists on truce.
newsitem.headline: Major pleads with Protestant extremists on truce.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major on Sunday pleaded with Protestant extremists in Northern Ireland not to end their ceasefire.
"Don't, Don't, Don't," he said in a direct appeal made in a BBC Television interview. "The IRA (Irish Republican Army) are isolated. Leave them isolated."

"At the moment, the IRA have isolated themselves by their own wickedness and their own violence. The Loyalists should not use that as an excuse for equal wickedness and violence," Major told Sir David Frost.
A member of Northern Ireland's pro-British guerrillas said on Saturday his organisation would end a two-year-old truce if its IRA foes killed anyone in its war to end British rule of the province.

A "senior Loyalist paramilitary source" told the Irish Times the outlawed Ulster Freedom Fighters (UFF) would launch a campaign against their pro-Irish nationalist adversaries if the IRA killed anyone in its latest campaign.

His comments increased fears that Loyalists, who want the province to remain British, might abandon their two-year-long truce because of IRA violence and return to the tit-for-tat war which killed 3,200 people in 27 years.
